candidates.proposition: The National Public Procurement Administration issued Notice No. 18 of 2027 mandating procurement eligibility review for memory components used in designated data-infrastructure projects, effective May 21, 2027.

Purchasing entities for designated data-infrastructure projects must conduct an eligibility review before placing, renewing, or releasing purchase orders for high-reliability memory modules, solid-state storage components, and integrated memory assemblies listed in Annex III; items failing the review shall not receive a new purchase release.

Project operators must complete a review of open, undelivered procurement records within ten working days of the notice's effective date, recording cancellation or substitution decisions for pending releases that fail eligibility.
candidates.subject_time: Within ten working days of May 21, 2027

candidates.proposition: Implementation reports received by the Administration identify cancellations of pending Micron memory-component releases associated with designated data-infrastructure projects and the movement of corresponding requirements to alternative approved supply arrangements.
The implementation reports do not state a common product code, a common customer name, or a common reason across the individual Micron cancellation entries.
Notice No. 18 of 2027 does not direct project operators to halt operating systems or remove already-installed equipment.

Annex III defines 'designated data-infrastructure project' to include public-cloud data-service projects together with 'other corresponding infrastructure uses,' containing several project formulations not reproduced in the earlier public summary of the notice.

Purchasing entities shall not infer a supplier's eligibility from past delivery to a different project class; a prior delivery record may be considered only alongside project-specific review materials required by Annex III.
